verified_claims: For a cut from C to an interior point of AB, the two child angle triples are (A, x, 180-A-x) and (B, C-x, A+x), and every strict split 0<x<C is geometrically realizable.

When 180=n theta with n>=3, either an angle is already a positive integral multiple of theta or the largest-angle construction produces a legal cut for which both possible retained children contain complementary positive integral multiples of theta.
Splitting an angle m theta into theta and (m-1) theta gives a well-founded descent and forces termination after finitely many cuts, with the stated uniform bound.
The separate n=2 construction is legal for every non-right triangle and forces a right angle in both children.
When 180/theta is not an integer, the equilateral starting triangle is clean, and the exhaustive four-pairing argument proves that Shan-Yu can retain a clean child after every cut.
The clean-child strategy has the correct adversarial quantifiers and prevents a target angle at every finite stage; possible limiting degeneration is irrelevant.

The finite-lattice program was rerun for totals 3 through 60 and returned exactly the divisor targets in all 1769 parameter pairs; the candidate appropriately does not use this computation as proof of the real-angle result.
The manifest accurately summarizes the proof, assumptions, and evidentiary status of the computation.
summary: The classification theta=180 degrees/n for integers n>=2 is proved correctly and completely. No counterexample, hidden quantifier shift, illegal or degenerate cut, circular step, or unjustified analytic claim was found.
transfer_assessment: Reusable: encode a geometric cut by an exact strict angle split and write both adversarial successor states explicitly.
